Team, below is my rough engineering-level sizing and the assumptions. I tried to be explicit so sales/procurement have something defensible.

Short answer / recommendation
- For a 30B decoder model with 32k context serving streaming generation, we recommend an initial dedicated pool of 6 x H100-80GB (NVL-accelerated) as the conservative committed baseline, with a burst lane of +3 GPUs for traffic spikes. Why H100: better attention kernel throughput and NVLink for larger KV cache locality; A100 80GB could work but we lose margin on p99 for bursty token-by-token workloads.

Key assumptions (call out)
- Model memory: 30B params * 2 bytes (FP16) ~ 60 GB active model weights in memory. Additional ~8–12 GB for activation buffers and runtime workspace (depends on batch/beam).
- Quantization benefits (practical, depending on ops/ops-kernels): int8 (AMPQ/LLM.int8) reduces weights by ~2x in practice (so model footprint to ~30–35 GB); 4-bit quant (Q4_K_M etc) reduces to ~20 GB or ~30% of FP16 in best-case when kernels are supported. Real-world overhead for dequant/compute increases compute cost ~5–15% and sometimes increases transient activation memory — call that out in the workbook.
- KV cache sizing: KV cache ~= (hidden_size * 2 * num_layers) * context_length * bytes_per_element. For a 30B model, assume hidden_size ~ 12k and num_layers ~ 40 (these are example numbers—ask Orion for exact topology). With 32k tokens and 2 bytes per element (FP16), KV cache per concurrent request can approach ~ (12k * 2 * 40) * 32k * 2 bytes ~ 73 GB — this is why 32k contexts drive large per-request memory. If using int8/4-bit KV cache formats we can reduce KV storage by ~2–4x, but that requires specialized kernels and validation.
- Concurrent sessions per GPU: with H100-80GB and FP16 model + KV cache, expect ~1–2 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU at low-latency p99 targets. With int8 model + compact KV cache formats, we can target ~3–5 concurrent sessions per GPU.

Suggested fleet (conservative)
- Committed: 6 x H100-80GB (for baseline sustained throughput ~30–45 qps assuming average tokens per request ~350 and careful batching + prefix caching). This assumes we route heavier long-context sessions to dedicated nodes with pre-warmed KV caches.
- Burst pool: +3 H100-80GB (on-demand/auto-burst in same cluster) to handle peak events.
- If Orion can quantize model to int8 and adopt compact KV cache, the committed pool could drop to ~3–4 H100-80GB equivalence. 4-bit could further reduce to 2–3 GPUs but requires validation for quality/regression.

Operational notes
- Pre-warming KV cache: for long-context, we recommend JWT-based routing and prefix caching to avoid reconstructing huge KV caches on every request. Warm caches for repeating session prefixes and maintain LRU eviction tuned to memory.
- Fallback policy: keep a smaller FP16 pool for cold starts and to serve requests that fail quantized kernels.
- Benchmarks required: we need a sample model binary and a replay of representative traffic for final numbers. We'll produce a workbook with sensitivity rows for context length (8k/16k/32k), quantization (FP16/int8/Q4), and p99 latency targets.

I attached a quick CSV with KV cache estimate lines and a draft fleet_cost_model_v3.xlsx. I recommend we validate int8 first; if quality is acceptable then we can go forward with a smaller committed purchase.

Aditya Rao
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
